Subject: Hyperlane: prioritized model-affinity + cold-start guards

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Hyperlane's performance numbers look solid and the team is aligned on moving to a Q3 pilot, contingent on two feature risk items we flagged during the call. I wanted to put the ask in writing and request an internal prioritization with Product/Eng. High level: Hyperlane needs deterministic model affinity and cold-start guard rails for regulatory traceability and to meet their SLA for peak trading hours.

Why this matters (customer POV):
- They require per-tenant route affinity so audit logs map requests to a stable model version for compliance.
- Their peak window has bursty traffic; cold-model starts currently introduce latency spikes outside their SLA (~95th p99).
- They will sign a reserved capacity commitment (deal HL-3921) if we can commit to a Q3 timeline and a small one-time engineering migration effort.

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate scheduling this as a prioritized workstream (canary -> canary+rollout) for Q3? Specific deliverables requested by the customer:
1) Model affinity toggle (per-tenant pin to model version, with audit log entries).
2) Cold-start guard that pre-warms key model weights/kv cache before peak windows.
3) Acceptance criteria / test harness we can run during pilot.

I've attached a one-page ask and the POC run summary. If we can get an approximate level-of-effort and a rough delivery window, I can update Hyperlane and tie it to the mutual action plan.

Attachments: [attachment: hyperlane-feature-ask-v2.pdf (PDF, 88KB)], [attachment: hyperlane-poc-results.csv (CSV, 46KB)]

Thanks —
Evelyn

Thanks for the context, Evelyn. I reviewed the attachments quickly and spoke with Ben offline. High-level take: this is a reasonable enterprise ask and aligns with our compliance-driven activation playbook, but we need to scope trade-offs.

Initial engineering options (very rough):
- Option A (routing table pin): implement a per-tenant routing table that maps route -> model-binary-id. Pros: explicit auditability, lower runtime overhead. Cons: changes to routing layer, requires migration for pinned tenants. Estimated LOE: 3-4 sprints (1 FE, 2 BE). Risk: medium.
- Option B (annotation+sticky cache): keep current routing but annotate requests and bias placement to a preferred variant; rely on sticky KV cache pre-warm. Pros: lower infra churn. Cons: weaker guarantee of 100% affinity. Estimated LOE: 2-3 sprints. Risk: medium-low.
- Cold-start pre-warm: independent piece. Could be implemented as scheduled cache seeding for tenant groups. Estimated LOE: 1-2 sprints. Risk: low.

Questions for Sales/CS to finalize:
1) Can Hyperlane accept Option B (weaker hard guarantee) if we provide stronger audit entries and a runbook for their compliance team?
2) Which exact windows should pre-warm target (Sara, you mentioned 02:00-03:30 UTC — confirm).
3) Will Hyperlane run acceptance tests or do we need to provide the harness? (We can provide both but need to budget for test automation).

Next steps proposed:
- Ben to produce a short technical note with final LOE and a prioritized backlog by EOW (next Fri).
- Product to tentatively tag this as "sales-advocacy P1" for Q3 pending engineering confirmation.
- Evelyn to confirm timeline pressure with Hyperlane and link to mutual action plan.

Ben — can you post the technical note in the shared drive (link in reply) and include any infra blockers? Karthik — if you foresee infra constraints (affinity state, residency), flag them here so we can escalate.

Marissa
